bottom_line: In MERIT-HF, metoprolol CR/XL once daily vs placebo lowered all-cause mortality (relative risk 0.66 [95% CI 0.53–0.81]).
implications: The reported relative risk for all-cause mortality (0.66 [95% CI 0.53–0.81]) supports that, in this study population and follow-up, metoprolol CR/XL was associated with lower all-cause mortality than placebo. The document also reports reductions in sudden death (0.59 [0.45–0.78]) and death from aggravated heart failure (0.51 [0.33–0.79]). The document notes few NYHA class IV patients, so efficacy and safety in severe chronic heart failure are not established here.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomised controlled study in chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) with ejection fraction ≤0.40.
major_points.quote: We enrolled 3991 patients with chronic heart failure in New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class II–IV and with ejection fraction of 0·40 or less, stabilised with optimum standard therapy, in a double-blind randomised controlled study.

major_points.text: Randomisation was preceded by a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in period.
major_points.quote: Randomisation was preceded by a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in period.

major_points.text: Participants were assigned metoprolol CR/XL (n=1990) or placebo (n=2001), starting at 12.5 mg or 25 mg once daily with target dose 200 mg once daily.
major_points.quote: 1990 patients were randomly assigned metoprolol CR/XL 12·5 mg (NYHA III–IV) or 25·0 mg once daily (NYHA II) and 2001 were assigned placebo. The target dose was 200 mg once daily and doses were up-titrated over 8 weeks.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality analysed by intention to treat.
major_points.quote: Our primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analysed by intention to treat.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with metoprolol CR/XL than placebo with RR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53–0.81).
major_points.quote: All-cause mortality was lower in the metoprolol CR/XL group than in the placebo group (145 [7·2%, per patient-year of follow-up]) vs 217 deaths [11·0 %], relative risk 0·66 [95% CI 0·53–0·81]

major_points.text: Study was stopped early on recommendation of the independent safety committee; mean follow-up time was 1 year.
major_points.quote: The study was stopped early on the recommendation of the independent safety committee. Mean follow-up time was 1 year.

absolute_effects.text: All-cause mortality: 145 (7.2%, per patient-year of follow-up) vs 217 deaths (11.0 %).
absolute_effects.quote: All-cause mortality was lower in the metoprolol CR/XL group than in the placebo group (145 [7·2%, per patient-year of follow-up]) vs 217 deaths [11·0 %]
There were fewer sudden deaths in the metoprolol CR/XL group than in the placebo group (79 vs 132, 0·59 [0·45–0·78]; p=0·0002)

absolute_effects.text: Death from aggravated heart failure: 30 vs 58.
absolute_effects.quote: Death from aggravated heart failure occurred in 30 patients in the actively treated group and in 58 patients in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Number needed to treat: 27 patients treated for 1 year to prevent one death.
absolute_effects.quote: Therefore, treatment of 27 patients with metoprolol CR/XL for 1 year can prevent one death.

subgroups.text: No significant increase in risk was seen in any predefined subgroups analysed for safety.
subgroups.quote: No significant increase in risk was seen in any of the predefined subgroups, analysed for safety (figure 5).

subgroups.text: Prespecified risk groups were defined by entry characteristics including tertiles for several continuous variables and categories for other characteristics.
subgroups.quote: We used Cox’s proportional hazards regression analyses of total mortality to explore any unfavourable outcome in prespecified risk groups, defined by entry characteristics.

subgroups.text: Post-hoc analysis evaluated mortality and mode of death in relation to NYHA functional class at randomisation.
subgroups.quote: In a post-hoc analysis, we analysed total mortality and mode of death in relation to NYHA functional class at randomisation.

harms.text: Permanent early discontinuation occurred in 13.9% with metoprolol CR/XL vs 15.3% with placebo.
harms.quote: Study drug was permanently stopped early in 13·9% of the metoprolol CR/XL group and in 15·3% of the placebo group (0·90 [0·77–1·06]).

harms.text: No patient was lost to follow-up.
harms.quote: No patient was lost to follow-up (figure 1).

guidelines_referenced.text: Steering Committee and membership of the Advisory Council to Improve Outcomes Nationwide in Heart Failure. Consensus recommendations for the management of chronic heart failure.
guidelines_referenced.quote: Steering Committee and membership of the Advisory Council to Improve Outcomes Nationwide in Heart Failure. Consensus recommendations for the management of chronic heart failure. Am J Cardiol 1999; 83: 2–38A.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were men and women, aged 40–80 years,

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptomatic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) for 3 months or more before randomisation.
inclusion_criteria.quote: who had had symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] functional class II–IV) for 3 months or more before randomisation

inclusion_criteria.text: Receiving optimum standard therapy at enrolment, defined as any combination of diuretics and an ACE inhibitor.
inclusion_criteria.quote: who were receiving optimum standard therapy at enrolment (2 weeks before randomisation), defined as any combination of diuretics and an ACE inhibitor.

inclusion_criteria.text: Stable clinical condition during the 2-week run-in phase between enrolment and randomisation.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Other inclusion criteria were a stable clinical condition during the 2-week run-in phase between enrolment and randomisation

inclusion_criteria.text: Left-ventricular ejection fraction of 0.40 or lower within 3 months before enrolment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: and a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 0·40 or lower within 3 months before enrolment.

inclusion_criteria.text: Supine resting heart rate had to be 68 beats per min or more at enrolment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Supine resting heart rate had to be 68 beats per min or more at enrolment.

exclusion_criteria.text: Acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 28 days before randomisation.
exclusion_criteria.quote: The exclusion criteria were: acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 28 days before randomisation;

exclusion_criteria.text: Indication or contraindication for treatment with b-blockade or drugs with β-blocking properties such as amiodarone.
exclusion_criteria.quote: indication or contraindication for treatment with b-blockade or drugs with β-blocking properties such as amiodarone;

exclusion_criteria.text: Use of amiodarone within 6 months before enrolment.
exclusion_criteria.quote: use of amiodarone within 6 months before enrolment;

exclusion_criteria.text: Unstable decompensated heart failure (pulmonary oedema, hypoperfusion) or supine systolic blood pressure lower than 100 mm Hg at enrolment.
exclusion_criteria.quote: unstable decompensated heart failure (pulmonary oedema, hypoperfusion) or supine systolic blood pressure lower than 100 mm Hg at enrolment;

exclusion_criteria.text: Poor compliance, defined as more than a 25% deviation of the number of observed compared with number of expected consumed placebo tablets during the run-in period.
exclusion_criteria.quote: poor compliance, defined as more than a 25% deviation of the number of observed compared with number of expected consumed placebo tablets during the run-in period.

analysis_methods.text: Power calculation assumed significance level a=0.04 (two-sided) for all-cause mortality with intention-to-treat analysis; at least 80% power.
analysis_methods.quote: This calculation was based on a significance level of a=0·04 for all-cause mortality (two-sided, intention to treat, a=0·01 was used for the second primary endpoint) and a power of at least 80% (b<0·20)

analysis_methods.text: Predetermined interim analyses were done when 25%, 50%, and 75% of expected total deaths had occurred.
analysis_methods.quote: predetermined interim analyses, done when 25%, 50%, and 75% of expected total deaths had occurred.

analysis_methods.text: Main analyses used log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model to calculate relative risks and 95% CI.
analysis_methods.quote: For the main analyses we used the log-rank test to compare the two groups, and Cox’s proportional hazards model to calculate relative risks and 95% CI.

analysis_methods.text: Analysis was by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: Analysis was by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: A second p value for total mortality was calculated adjusted for the two predefined interim analyses.
analysis_methods.quote: We calculated a second p value for total mortality adjusted for the two predefined interim analyses

trial_conduct.text: The study was approved by local ethics committees.
trial_conduct.quote: The study was approved by local ethics committees.

trial_conduct.text: All patients gave written informed consent.
trial_conduct.quote: All patients gave written informed consent.

trial_conduct.text: Independent endpoint committee blinded to treatment status classified all deaths using prespecified definitions.
trial_conduct.quote: An independent endpoint committee, whose members were unaware of treatment status, classified all deaths according to prespecified definitions from medical records and other documents.

trial_conduct.text: Safety was monitored by an independent safety committee during the study.
trial_conduct.quote: Safety was monitored by an independent safety committee during the study.

trial_conduct.text: International steering committee stopped the study after the second preplanned interim analysis (50%) met the predefined stopping criterion (Z=3.807 vs boundary 2.98).
trial_conduct.quote: The international steering committee stopped the study on Oct 31, 1998, on the recommendation of the independent safety committee. The second preplanned interim analysis (50%) showed that the predefined criterion for ending the study had been met and exceeded (Z=3·807 vs a boundary value of 2·98).

funding_declarations.text: Astra Hässle AB, Mölndal, Sweden, sponsored the study.
funding_declarations.quote: Astra Hässle AB, Mölndal, Sweden, sponsored the study

criticisms.text: Few patients were included in NYHA functional class IV, so efficacy and safety in severe chronic heart failure remains to be assessed.
criticisms.quote: We included few patients in NYHA functional class IV. The efficacy and safety of b-blocker treatment in patients with severe chronic heart failure therefore remains to be assessed.

criticisms.text: Study was not powered for a separate analysis of mortality in patients with mild heart failure (NYHA class II).
criticisms.quote: Although our study was not powered for a separate analysis of mortality in patients with mild heart failure, the data are in accordance with a survival benefit also in this subgroup.

criticisms.text: Study was not designed or powered for a separate analysis of idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and did not include patients younger than 40 years.
criticisms.quote: Our study was not designed or powered for a separate analysis of patients with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and did not include patients younger than 40 years.

criticisms.text: Study was not designed to assess mechanisms underlying sudden death in chronic heart failure.
criticisms.quote: This study was not designed to assesss these mechanisms further.
